conventions.convention: M = R³ minus {0}; dν = d³k/(2|k|); the transverse Hilbert pairing is conjugate-linear in its first argument. Packets are normalized in this weighted measure.
The propagation axis is positive z, 0 < θmax < π/2, and 0 < κ− < κ+ < infinity. Paraxiality means the aperture limit θmax ↓ 0, rather than every fixed forward cone being a small-angle approximation.
h = i(n × ·), Pσ = (P + σh)/2, and eσᴺ = exp(iσφ)(eθ + iσeφ)/√2. Integer ℓ labels the scalar coefficient exp(iℓφ) in this north gauge; it is not a global orbital label.
U(Rz(t))f(k) = Rz(t)f(Rz(−t)k) = exp(−itJz/ℏ)f(k), so the north-gauge vortex has Jz eigenvalue (ℓ + σ)ℏ.
The conversion identity assumes a unitary U with U(D(Jz)) = D(Jz) and JzUψ = UJzψ on D(Jz). It assumes neither cone preservation nor helicity preservation.
The example adopts c = 1, radial phase exp(−it|k|), and E₀(f) = ℏ∫|k||f|²dν. These are mathematical model quantities, with no apparatus or empirical measurement asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. A normalized helicity-σ packet is a unit transverse vector supported in κ− ≤ |k| ≤ κ+ and 0 ≤ θ ≤ θmax, with Pσf = f almost everywhere. The north helicity gauge is smooth through the positive axis; its scalar winding ℓ is patch-dependent.

Assume AC and Countable Choice, with 0 < κ− < κ+ and 0 < θ₁ < θ₂ < θmax < π/2. For each σ = ±1 and ℓ ∈ Z, smooth real compactly supported radial and angular bumps exist. For any such bumps a,b, the packet a(r)b(θ)exp(iℓφ)eσᴺ/√(πAB), with A = ∫r|a|²dr and B = ∫sinθ|b|²dθ, belongs to the smooth transverse domain, has norm one and helicity σ, and satisfies Jzf = (ℓ + σ)ℏf.

Under AC and Countable Choice, every normalized helicity-σ packet in the stated cone satisfies ⟨S′z⟩ = ℏσ∫cosθ|f|²dν and |⟨S′z⟩ − ℏσ| ≤ ℏ(1 − cosθmax) ≤ ℏθmax²/2. For the constructed north-gauge vortex, ⟨L′z⟩ = ℓℏ + ℏσ(1 − ∫cosθ|f|²dν), with |⟨L′z⟩ − ℓℏ| ≤ ℏθmax²/2.

Exact countable-choice hypothesis carried by the Hilbert-space and measure suppliers.

Construction of radial and angular interval bumps by restricting a translated three-dimensional bump.

Separation of finite-support normalization integrals and null-surface integrals on finite annuli.
|sin u| ≤ |u| in the quadratic aperture estimate.
Cosine double-angle identity in the spin-error estimate.
Cosine decreases on [0,π] and lies in [−1,1], allowing the pointwise cone bound.
